wa_pit_the_3.blurb: The Pit is a compact sport-climbing wall inside the Deep Creek complex, a short drive northwest of Spokane. It holds about twenty bolted lines and is a hard-climber's venue: most routes land in the 5.11 range, with a solid block of 5.12 and 5.13 and a lone 5.10 and 5.14 at the edges. Expect steep, powerful climbing on columnar basalt, and watch for loose pillars and scattered rubble underfoot, so helmets and sturdy approach shoes make sense. The wall tends to dry out ahead of the bigger faces nearby, which makes it a handy early-year choice. Little here suits a beginner.

_expect.name: NW End - Honeycomb and Anarchy Walls

wa_nw_end_honeycomb_and_anarchy_walls.blurb: This is the northwest corner of Last Wall, a long cliff band in McLoughlin Canyon outside Tonasket in Okanogan County. Around twenty routes are split between bolted lines (twelve) and gear climbs (eight), covering an unusually friendly spread: a handful of very easy pitches, a middle band in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, and the bulk at 5.10 with a few 5.11s. The Anarchy Wall in particular offers short, gentle leads suited to newer leaders, while the Honeycomb Wall is steeper and cleaner low down. Rattlesnakes are common near the base in warm weather, so keep an eye on dogs and children.

wa_gritscone.blurb: Gritscone is a very small wall near North Bend, the first crag reached on the trail toward Dirty Harry's Peak in the Far Side group off I-90. Its roughly twenty routes are almost all bolted, with a couple of trad lines and one boulder problem, running from the easiest grades up to 5.11. Most sit between 5.6 and 5.10, mostly lower-angle face climbing with a few jug hauls and some tougher overhanging bits. Lines are short with few bolts and can usually be top-roped by walking around, which makes this a popular beginner and class venue. Dense forest keeps it shaded and slow to dry.

wa_bend_west.blurb: Bend West is the busiest section of The Bend, a cliff above a curve in the Tieton River west of Yakima. Most of its twenty routes are trad, with a few bolted lines, and the climbing is mainly crack-oriented. Grades centre on 5.9 and 5.10, with a handful of 5.11s and a few easier leads, so it suits climbers who are comfortable placing gear at the 5.10 level. A dozen or so good lines are packed close together, and the wall sits in shade through the morning before the sun swings round later in the day. Rattlesnakes live along the approach.

wa_dana_s_arch_area.blurb: Dana's Arch Area is a section of the Upper Town Wall above the town of Index, in the Skykomish valley. It is known for long, sustained lines, several of them multi-pitch, mixing gear-protected and bolted climbing, plus a single aid route. The twenty routes here are mostly trad (eleven) with eight sport lines, and the difficulty sits well up the scale: the majority fall at 5.11, a good number reach 5.12, and a few go harder still. It is a destination for experienced climbers wanting committing, high-quality wall climbing rather than a place for first leads.

wa_millennium_wall.blurb: Millennium Wall is one of the cliffs in the Sunshine's Lower Cliffs group at Frenchman Coulee, near Vantage on the Columbia River. Nearly all of its twenty routes are bolted single pitches, with just one trad line. The grades are friendly to the middle of the range: a few 5.7 and 5.8s, a good number of 5.9s, and the biggest cluster at 5.10, with only one 5.11. The streaked, orange-and-white basalt gives steady, moderate sport climbing, and difficulty tends to creep upward as you move east along the wall. Neighbouring walls are only minutes away.

wa_old_school_wall.blurb: Old School Wall sits within Ozone, a popular single-pitch cliff in the Columbia Gorge on the Washington side, east of Vancouver. With twenty routes it is one of the largest walls there, and it is mostly a gear wall: thirteen trad lines to seven sport. Grades are moderate throughout, centred on 5.8 through 5.10, with a few easier lines at the bottom and a single 5.11. That makes it a good place for climbers building up to harder leads, and a good fit for a mixed trad and sport partnership. The cliff in general is well shaded, so it stays comfortable on warm days.

wa_bouldering_2.blurb: McLellan Rocks is a granite bouldering area in Riverside State Park, on the south side of the Spokane River past Nine Mile Falls. Boulders and small domes are scattered through open ponderosa pine forest, giving a relaxed, pleasant setting. Problems here range from V1 up to V10, with the bulk in the V4 to V6 band, a respectable group at V8 and V9, and only a few easy ones, so it favours intermediate and strong boulderers. Most lines face east or west, so you can chase shade or sun depending on the day. Summers run hot and mosquitoes can be thick in early summer.
